key_insight: Bayesian inference fused with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulation can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade—at the electron interface, hole interface, or in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This approach helps engineers diagnose failure mechanisms in finished devices and target interface passivation or materials design to improve long-term stability.
method: Photoluminescence imaging captures spatially resolved optoelectronic behavior across the device.
Drift-diffusion simulations link image features to recombination-related parameters.
Bayesian inference produces time-evolving parameter maps during aging (70 °C, full-spectrum sunlight).
evidence_signal: The authors tracked inferred parameter maps during accelerated aging and found strong spatial heterogeneity, with the largest degradation concentrated at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: Because the inference depends on model assumptions and image-to-parameter mapping, incorrect physics in the drift-diffusion model could bias the inferred degradation site.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
